_comment: Cross-boundary architecture manifest (#124; governance PIPELINE_GOVERNANCE_AND_STATE §10). The DECLARED ground truth for the couplings NO import tool sees — external-process invocations, cross-language dispatch, guarded entry points, and client<->server rule boundaries. tests/test_arch_manifest.py asserts the real code matches this manifest; a NEW undeclared edge FAILS the suite. This is the fitness-function layer that complements import-linter (intra-Python) + dependency-cruiser (intra-Node), which see imports only. Update this file DELIBERATELY when you add such an edge — that edit is the review surface for a new cross-boundary coupling.

external_programs._comment: Every external program the acquisition pipeline shells out to (argv[0] of a subprocess argv-list, whether via subprocess.* directly or the injectable _run seam). test_no_undeclared_external_program scans argv-list literals and asserts each program is declared here.

claude.why: Stage 2 Wave-2 discovery — `claude -p` print mode with WebSearch (the speculative residual index).

node.why: Stage 3 capture — Python->Node Playwright dispatch (the cross-LANGUAGE edge).

pdftotext.why: PDF -> layout text (poppler). Stage 4 harvest + Stage 5 handbook page slice.

pdftoppm.why: PDF -> raster PNG for OCR (poppler). Stage 4.

pdfinfo.why: PDF page count (poppler). Stage 5 handbook slice sizing.

entry_point_guards._comment: An invariant guard that MUST be reached by every listed entry point — the fix for the class of bug where a rule is enforced at one entry point (the console) but a sibling (the CLI) skips it. #198 review finding #2: the headless CLI run_batch ran a terminal abandoned batch because the guard lived only in the console. test_entry_point_guards_are_called asserts the guard call appears in each function body.
entry_point_guards.why: #168: never run a pipeline stage on a terminal `abandoned` batch (its schools are excluded from the attempted-set; running it re-queues them — the #162 poison).

client_server_boundaries._comment: Rules about the browser-JS <-> server boundary — a class the import graphs can't see at all.

forbidden_client_comparisons._comment: A server-authoritative rule literal must NOT be re-decided in client JS by COMPARISON (it duplicates a server truth and drifts). #198 review finding #3: the gate@6 benchmark badge keyed on `c.batch_id === 'batch_00000'` instead of the server-computed `is_benchmark` (batch_type='benchmark'), so a second benchmark batch would be walled server-side but unbadged. Checked in COMPARISON context only (=== / !== / == / !=), so an incidental display string like `benchmark-walled (batch_00000)` is allowed.
forbidden_client_comparisons.use_instead: the server-computed `is_benchmark` field on the candidates payload (batch_type='benchmark')

single_definition_helpers._comment: A shared client helper must be defined in exactly ONE file (common.js) so its behavior can't fork across the stage views. #198 review finding #5: the abandoned-status badge tone was added to gate1.js only, leaving stage2/3/4.js rendering a retired batch in the neutral draft tone — fixed by centralizing statusBadge in common.js.
single_definition_helpers.name: statusBadge

file_dispatches._comment: The file-based stage handoffs — regenerable, auditable RECEIPTS (the DB is the working store; governance §1). Declared here for provenance; test_file_dispatch_producers_reference_artifact asserts each producer module actually references its artifact filename (a light contract that the declared producer is the real one). NOT the transport between stages.

receipts.role: per-district full per-school discovery audit trail
